visuals.heading: Fix Your Headline First

items.text: Whatever sits in that first stretch either gets you found or gets you skipped.
A strong-fit profile can sit on page 20 just as easily as page 2.

Recruiters using LinkedIn Recruiter typically build a keyword search across job titles, skills, summaries, and experience descriptions, then combine terms with AND, OR, and NOT to narrow a large pool down fast.
There is a second problem that even keyword-optimized profiles hit: search results are not ranked by how well you match.

blocks.heading: Works When You Have Limited Experience

items.text: Only the first two to three lines of your About section show before someone has to click "see more." Most people never click.
Use a five-part structure instead, and keep the whole section under roughly 200-250 words:
Open with your direction and a specific claim, not your college.

items.text: Your 2-3 strongest projects, linked directly, a GitHub repo, a live dashboard, a design file, a Google Doc case study.
A certificate that is genuinely relevant to your target role, not every certificate you have collected.
A short write-up (even a LinkedIn post) explaining what a project solved and what you learned building it.

blocks.heading: Connecting Strategically: How to Network Without Spam-Connecting

items.text: Line 1: Who you are and the specific, shared reason you are reaching out, same college, same target role, a post they wrote.
Line 2: One honest, specific thing you want, advice on breaking into a role, a quick question about their work, not a job ask on day one.
Line 3: A low-pressure close that makes it easy to say yes, even briefly.
Set visibility to "Recruiters only," not "All LinkedIn members", this shares your status with hiring professionals without putting a green frame on your photo for your entire network to see.
Fill in the target roles, locations, and start date fields inside the Open to Work form accurately, this is what recruiters actually filter by, not the badge itself.
Keep engaging normally: commenting on posts in your field, congratulating connections, sharing something you built.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Quietly Kill Fresher Profiles

items.text: Headline that only says "Student" or "Fresher | Actively looking," wasting the most-searched real estate on the profile.
About section opening with college and degree instead of a specific, provable claim.
Projects and internships listed as bare titles with no task or outcome described.
Mass-sending blank connection requests, then wondering why nobody replies.
Open to Work set to "All LinkedIn members" without realizing the badge is visible to everyone, including current professors or part-time employers.
